skill: Classify a small linear system as inconsistent, consistent dependent, or consistent independent, then select exactly the true class statement using the observed checkbox or Roman-statement radio contract.
reasoning_steps: Read coefficients and constants as an augmented matrix.
Use Gaussian elimination to expose a contradiction or determine pivots and free variables.
A contradiction gives no solutions; otherwise full column rank gives one solution and a free variable gives infinitely many.
Map the classification to the displayed wording and selection control.
invariants: Linear equations in two or three variables; small integer or simple rational entries.
Three mutually exclusive classifications; no requirement to enter the general solution.
Preserve full observed banks, including optional None of the above and radio distractors.
Moderate workload: short elimination, contradiction or free-variable interpretation; no parameter solving.
permitted_variations: Change coefficients and RHS together or separately, permitting consistency to change within a fixed shape.
For 2/3, dependent and inconsistent are eligible; unique is impossible. For 2/2 and 3/2 all three classes are eligible.
Change dependent row, contradiction location, pivot positions, row order, signs, simple rational scalings and consistent solution values while keeping workload small.
Permute statement roles and option positions independently of the class. The source's qualifying Roman label or specific class per example is incidental, not essential.
Keep one true statement when the bank states the three disjoint classes; a fixed count here follows mathematics, unlike a fixed label.
